TITLE: Tax Act 2003
ACTNUMBER: 2003 No 47
TYPE: Act
STATUS: In force
VERSION: Latest
VERSIONTITLE: as at 17 September 2026
AGENCY: Ministry of Finance; and HM Treasury
DATEOFASSENT: 18 December 2003
COMMENCEMENT: see section 2

NOTE: This consolidated text contains original provisions and provisions inserted, substituted, relocated, repealed, and preserved by successive amendments. The principal Act deliberately retains its accumulated structure rather than separating each tax into a standalone Part. Lettered sections occur throughout the Act because later amendments have inserted provisions into established numerical sequences.

PARTNUMBER: 1
PARTTITLE: Preliminary Provisions
SECTION: 1
HEADING: Short title
1. This Act is the Tax Act 2003.
2. The Act may be cited as the Tax Act 2003 and, together with any regulations, Orders in Council, notices, determinations, and schedules made under it, forms part of the revenue law of Square Country.
3. A reference in an enactment, instrument, return, assessment, agreement, or other document to the Tax Act is, unless the context otherwise requires, a reference to this Act.
4. The short title does not limit the application of any provision of this Act or the operation of an amendment made to it.

SECTION: 2
HEADING: Commencement
1. This Act comes into force on 1 April 2004.
2. Different provisions of this Act may commence on different dates if this Act or an Order in Council made under an express power in this Act so provides.
3. A provision that is expressed to apply from the beginning of a tax year applies to transactions, amounts, events, and circumstances occurring during that tax year, whether or not the relevant assessment is made after that year.
4. A provision that imposes a tax, duty, levy, or excise must not be applied to a period before the commencement expressly authorised for that provision.
5. The Commissioner may publish commencement guidance identifying the first return period, payment date, registration date, or other administrative date affected by a commencement provision.
6. The publication of guidance under subsection 5 does not alter the legal effect of this Act.

SECTION: 3
HEADING: Purpose
1. The purposes of this Act are—
   (a) to impose and administer the taxes, duties, levies, and excises authorised by Parliament;
   (b) to provide rules for calculating, assessing, collecting, refunding, and recovering those amounts;
   (c) to provide a coherent framework for income, consumption, company, financial, resource, environmental, transport, customs, and other revenue regimes; and
   (d) to provide appropriate administrative, review, enforcement, and information-gathering powers.
2. The Act must be read as a whole, and the purpose of a particular provision must be considered in the context of the Part, subpart, section, and revenue regime in which the provision occurs.
3. A provision imposing liability must not be extended beyond its text merely because an amount or transaction appears economically similar to an amount or transaction expressly made subject to tax.
4. A provision granting a credit, refund, exemption, remission, deduction, concession, or other relief must be applied according to its terms and subject to any conditions attached to that relief.

SECTION: 4
HEADING: Act binds the Crown
1. This Act binds the Crown.
2. A Crown entity, department, office, agency, statutory corporation, or other public body is liable under this Act to the extent that the provision imposing the liability applies to it.
3. A Crown entity is not entitled to an exemption merely because it is owned, controlled, funded, or administered by the Crown unless the exemption is expressly provided by this Act or another enactment.
4. The Commissioner may determine administrative arrangements for dealings between Crown agencies where those arrangements do not alter the amount of tax legally imposed.

SECTION: 5
HEADING: Application of Act
1. This Act applies to every person, transaction, supply, importation, activity, asset, payment, and other matter that falls within a charging or administrative provision of the Act.
2. A provision applies only to the extent stated in the provision, and a reference to a person includes a body corporate, partnership, trust, estate, public authority, and other entity where the context permits.
3. Where 2 or more Parts apply to the same matter, each Part applies according to its terms unless one provision expressly modifies, limits, or displaces the other.
4. An amount must not be taxed twice merely because the same transaction gives rise to different administrative consequences, but this subsection does not prevent Parliament from imposing separate taxes on the same transaction or activity under separate charging provisions.

SECTION: 6
HEADING: Relationship with other enactments
1. This Act applies subject to any later enactment that expressly amends, overrides, or disapplies a provision of this Act.
2. A reference to another enactment is a reference to that enactment as amended from time to time unless this Act expressly provides otherwise.
3. If an inconsistency arises between this Act and another enactment concerning the administration of a tax imposed by this Act, the specific provision governing that tax prevails to the extent of the inconsistency.
4. Nothing in this section authorises the Commissioner to disregard an enactment merely because compliance with it would produce an inconvenient, unexpected, or commercially unusual result.

SECTION: 7
HEADING: Interpretation Act and general rules
1. The Interpretation Act applicable in Square Country applies to this Act except to the extent that this Act expressly provides otherwise.
2. The meaning of a provision must be ascertained from its text and, where relevant, its purpose, context, history, and relationship with the other provisions of this Act.
3. A reference to the singular includes the plural and a reference to the plural includes the singular unless the context requires otherwise.
4. A reference to writing includes an electronic record capable of being retained and reproduced.
5. A reference to a day, month, quarter, or tax year is to be determined in accordance with the applicable provision of this Act.
6. A reference to an amount includes an amount that is nil unless the context indicates that a positive amount is required.

SECTION: 8
HEADING: Administration of Act
1. The Commissioner is responsible for administering this Act.
2. The Commissioner must establish systems reasonably necessary for registration, filing, assessment, payment, collection, refund, audit, review, and recovery.
3. Administrative practice may facilitate compliance but must not amend, waive, or create a liability imposed by Parliament.
4. The Commissioner may issue public statements, forms, specifications, and operational guidance for the administration of this Act.
5. A statement or item of guidance does not bind a taxpayer where it is inconsistent with the Act.

SECTION: 9
HEADING: Commissioner of Revenue
1. The Commissioner of Revenue is the statutory officer responsible for the functions and powers conferred by this Act.
2. The Commissioner must exercise those powers fairly, consistently, and for the purposes for which they are conferred.
3. The Commissioner may establish specialised units for income tax, GST, digital taxation, customs, excise, resource levies, infrastructure charges, financial taxation, and revenue enforcement.
4. The establishment of a specialised unit does not transfer statutory responsibility away from the Commissioner.

SECTION: 10
HEADING: Delegation
1. The Commissioner may delegate a function or power under this Act to an officer of the Ministry of Finance & Revenue or another person authorised by law.
2. A delegation must be in writing and may be subject to conditions.
3. A delegate exercising a power must comply with any condition imposed by the Commissioner and must identify the delegation when required by this Act.
4. A delegation does not prevent the Commissioner from exercising the same function or power.
5. A person affected by a delegated decision retains any objection, review, or appeal right available under this Act.

SECTION: 11
HEADING: Tax year
1. The tax year begins on 1 April and ends on 31 March of the following year unless another provision specifies a different period.
2. A provision referring to a tax year applies to the year in which the relevant period ends unless the context requires otherwise.
3. The Commissioner may approve an alternative balance date for a person where another accounting period is more appropriate, subject to conditions imposed under this Act.
4. An approved alternative balance date does not of itself change the rate, threshold, exemption, or liability applicable to the person.

SECTION: 12
HEADING: Accounting periods
1. A person must calculate amounts for the accounting period required by the applicable revenue regime.
2. An accounting period may be a month, quarter, tax year, financial year, or other period prescribed by this Act.
3. Where an accounting period changes, the person must make any balancing, apportionment, or transitional adjustment required by this Act.
4. The Commissioner may require a person to reconcile overlapping accounting periods where necessary to prevent an amount from being omitted or counted more than once.

SECTION: 13
HEADING: Amounts expressed in money
1. An amount required to be expressed in money must be expressed in the currency of Square Country unless another currency is required by the provision.
2. A foreign currency amount must be converted using the exchange rate required by this Act or, if no rate is prescribed, a rate reasonably reflecting the relevant transaction date.
3. The Commissioner may approve an alternative exchange-rate method for a class of persons or transactions.
4. An approved method must be applied consistently unless the Commissioner permits a change.

SECTION: 14
HEADING: Rounding and fractions
1. An amount may be rounded only where this Act, a regulation, or an approved calculation method permits rounding.
2. A rate or fraction must not be rounded before the point at which the relevant calculation is required to be completed unless the applicable provision expressly permits it.
3. The Commissioner may specify the treatment of fractions of a monetary unit, measurement unit, distance unit, litre, kilogram, emission unit, or other statutory unit.

SECTION: 15
HEADING: Effect of regulations
1. Regulations may prescribe matters that this Act expressly authorises to be prescribed.
2. Regulations must not impose a tax, duty, levy, or excise that is not authorised by an Act of Parliament.
3. If a regulation is inconsistent with this Act, the Act prevails.
4. A regulation may prescribe forms, filing methods, records, technical standards, measurement methods, electronic systems, rates where expressly authorised, and other administrative matters.

SECTION: 16
HEADING: Tax not imposed except by authority of Parliament
1. A person is liable to a tax, duty, levy, or excise only if liability is imposed by an Act of Parliament.
2. An administrative notice, assessment, form, practice statement, or system setting does not itself create a liability.
3. The Commissioner must identify the charging provision supporting a material assessment where the assessment is challenged.
4. Nothing in this section limits a power to determine the amount of an existing liability.

SECTION: 17
HEADING: Relationship between general and specific provisions
1. A specific provision prevails over a general provision to the extent that the 2 provisions cannot operate together.
2. A provision expressed to apply despite another provision prevails to the extent of the express inconsistency.
3. A later provision does not impliedly repeal an earlier provision merely because the provisions deal with related subject matter.
4. Where 2 charging provisions independently impose liability, each applies unless one expressly excludes the other.
5. The Commissioner must not select between inconsistent provisions solely by reference to which provision produces the greater amount of revenue.

SECTION: 18
HEADING: Application to transactions spanning tax years
1. Where a transaction, arrangement, supply, payment, or activity extends across 2 or more tax years, the amount attributable to each year must be determined under the timing rules applicable to that matter.
2. A person must make reasonable adjustments where the final amount cannot be determined at the end of the first period.
3. A later adjustment must be reflected in the return, assessment, credit, refund, or payment period specified by this Act.
4. A timing rule in a specific revenue regime prevails over this section to the extent of any inconsistency.

SECTION: 19
HEADING: Effect of amendments
1. An amendment to this Act applies from the commencement date specified by the amending enactment.
2. An amendment does not alter a completed assessment, payment, refund, transaction, or liability unless the amending enactment expressly provides for retrospective or transitional application.
3. Savings and transitional provisions must be read with the amended provision so that liabilities arising under the former law are not unintentionally extinguished.
4. A reference in this Act to an amended provision includes its historical application where a transitional provision requires the former wording to continue to apply.

SECTION: 20
HEADING: Continuation of existing liabilities
1. The repeal, replacement, or amendment of a provision does not extinguish a liability, right, power, obligation, penalty, interest amount, or proceeding that arose before the relevant change unless the amending enactment expressly provides otherwise.
2. A return, assessment, objection, appeal, investigation, recovery proceeding, or enforcement action commenced under a former provision may continue under that provision to the extent required by a savings provision.
3. The Commissioner may use records obtained under a former provision for the administration of the corresponding current provision, subject to any statutory restriction on the use or disclosure of the information.

PARTNUMBER: 2
PARTTITLE: Interpretation
SECTION: 21
HEADING: Definitions
1. In this Act, unless the context otherwise requires, the following terms have the meanings given by this section.
   (a) Commissioner means the Commissioner of Revenue;
   (b) company includes a body corporate and an entity treated as a company under this Act;
   (c) consideration includes money, money's worth, a debt, a benefit, a service, or another thing of economic value;
   (d) taxpayer means a person who is liable, potentially liable, entitled to a credit or refund, or subject to an administrative obligation under this Act;
   (e) tax includes a tax, duty, levy, excise, charge, or other amount imposed under this Act;
   (f) return includes a return, statement, declaration, schedule, or electronic record required to be furnished under this Act.
2. A definition applying only to a particular Part or provision does not apply generally unless the provision expressly provides for that result.
3. A term not defined in this Act has its ordinary meaning, subject to any applicable rule of statutory interpretation.

SECTION: 22
HEADING: Person
1. Person includes an individual, company, partnership, trust, estate, Crown entity, public authority, association, and other body or entity recognised by law.
2. A reference to a person acting in a capacity includes a trustee, executor, administrator, receiver, liquidator, agent, nominee, or representative.
3. A liability imposed on a person in a representative capacity is not a personal liability unless this Act expressly provides otherwise.
4. A reference to a class of persons may include a person who becomes a member of that class after the relevant transaction or event if the provision so provides.

SECTION: 23
HEADING: Connected persons
1. Persons are connected if the applicable provision treats their ownership, control, management, voting interests, economic dependence, family relationship, or other relationship as sufficient for connection.
2. The degree of connection required is determined by the provision in which the expression is used.
3. A commercial relationship does not of itself establish connection unless the applicable provision so provides.
4. The Commissioner may require information reasonably necessary to establish whether persons are connected for a particular provision.

SECTION: 24
HEADING: Amount
1. Amount includes a positive amount, a nil amount, a negative amount, a credit, a loss, or another quantified result where the context permits.
2. A reference to an amount derived, incurred, paid, received, supplied, imported, exported, or transferred includes an amount determined under a statutory formula.
3. An amount expressed in another currency must be converted in accordance with the applicable currency rule.

SECTION: 25
HEADING: Taxable period
1. Taxable period means the period for which liability is calculated under the applicable provision.
2. A taxable period may differ between revenue regimes, taxpayers, transactions, and classes of goods or services.
3. A person must not combine taxable periods merely because doing so would simplify administration unless the Commissioner permits the combination.

SECTION: 26
HEADING: Supply
1. Supply includes a supply of goods, services, property, rights, facilities, digital services, financial services, or another thing where a provision of this Act so provides.
2. A supply may occur whether or not consideration is paid at the same time.
3. A deemed supply under a charging provision is treated as a supply only for the purposes specified by that provision.

SECTION: 27
HEADING: Revenue account
1. A revenue account is an account, ledger, record, or statutory mechanism used to determine an amount payable, creditable, refundable, or otherwise attributable under this Act.
2. An amount recorded in a revenue account does not by itself establish a liability unless the operative provision so provides.
3. The Commissioner may prescribe the form and manner in which a revenue account is maintained.

SECTION: 28
HEADING: Assessment
1. Assessment means the determination by the Commissioner, a taxpayer, or another authorised person of an amount payable, refundable, creditable, or otherwise dealt with under this Act.
2. An assessment may be original, amended, estimated, default, provisional, final, or reassessed as provided by the relevant Part.
3. An assessment must identify the period and statutory basis on which it is made where required by this Act.

SECTION: 29
HEADING: Adjustment
1. Adjustment includes a correction, apportionment, reversal, reallocation, credit, debit, balancing amount, or other statutory change to an amount.
2. An adjustment must be made in the period required by the provision under which it arises.
3. A person must not make the same adjustment twice unless separate provisions independently require the adjustment.

SECTION: 30
HEADING: Exempt amount
1. An exempt amount is an amount that a provision expressly excludes from a charge, calculation, assessment, or other liability.
2. An exemption must be applied only to the extent specified by the provision granting it.
3. A person claiming an exemption must retain evidence sufficient to establish every condition on which the exemption depends.

SECTION: 31
HEADING: Credit
1. Credit includes an amount that may be offset against tax, duty, levy, excise, interest, penalty, or another amount where authorised by this Act.
2. A credit may be limited, carried forward, transferred, refunded, or cancelled under the applicable provision.
3. A credit must not be used to satisfy an unrelated liability unless this Act permits the use.

SECTION: 32
HEADING: Refund
1. Refund means payment by the Crown of an amount that a person is entitled to receive under this Act.
2. A refund may be withheld to the extent permitted by a provision allowing set-off against another amount owed by the person.
3. A refund entitlement does not arise merely because a person has made a payment unless the payment exceeds the amount properly payable or another provision expressly provides for a refund.

SECTION: 33
HEADING: Commissioner may determine
1. Where this Act authorises the Commissioner to determine an amount, fact, classification, rate, value, period, or other matter, the determination must be made on reasonable grounds.
2. The Commissioner may rely on information obtained from the taxpayer, another government agency, a financial institution, a customs record, an electronic system, or another lawful source.
3. A determination must not be used to impose a liability that the Act does not otherwise impose.

SECTION: 34
HEADING: Market value
1. Market value means the value determined in accordance with the applicable provision or, where no method is prescribed, a reasonable arm's-length value at the relevant time.
2. The Commissioner may take account of comparable transactions, independent valuations, published prices, commodity markets, exchange rates, and other reliable evidence.
3. A valuation method must be applied consistently unless the circumstances materially change.

SECTION: 35
HEADING: Arm's-length amount
1. An arm's-length amount is the amount that independent persons dealing with each other would reasonably have agreed having regard to the circumstances of the transaction.
2. The Commissioner may adjust an amount to an arm's-length amount where another provision expressly authorises the adjustment.
3. An adjustment must be supported by the facts and the statutory purpose of the provision authorising it.

PARTNUMBER: 3
PARTTITLE: Application and General Principles
SECTION: 36
HEADING: General charging principle
1. A person is liable for a tax, duty, levy, or excise only if the relevant charging provision applies to the person, amount, transaction, activity, or event.
2. A charging provision must be read with any exemption, threshold, deduction, credit, rate, timing rule, or special rule that forms part of the same regime.
3. Administrative provisions apply to a liability whether the amount is determined by the taxpayer or the Commissioner.

SECTION: 37
HEADING: Timing of liability
1. Liability arises at the time specified by the charging provision.
2. If no time is specified, the liability arises at the time the relevant transaction, payment, supply, importation, activity, or other event occurs.
3. A later assessment does not postpone the time at which a liability arose unless the Act expressly provides otherwise.

SECTION: 38
HEADING: Apportionment
1. An amount relating partly to one statutory treatment and partly to another must be apportioned on a reasonable basis.
2. The basis of apportionment must have regard to the nature and purpose of the amount and the circumstances in which it arose.
3. The Commissioner may prescribe an apportionment method for a class of persons or transactions.
4. A person using an approved method must retain sufficient records to demonstrate its application.

SECTION: 39
HEADING: No double counting
1. An amount must not be included twice in the same calculation merely because it is described differently in different records.
2. This section does not prevent separate taxes or charges from applying to the same transaction where Parliament has expressly imposed them.
3. Where an adjustment reverses an amount previously included, the reversal must be made in the period required by the applicable provision.

SECTION: 40
HEADING: Interaction of revenue regimes
1. The application of one revenue regime does not prevent another regime from applying unless an express exclusion applies.
2. The Commissioner must identify the statutory basis for each separate liability where a transaction gives rise to more than one assessment.
3. An exemption under one regime does not create an exemption under another regime unless the other regime expressly adopts the exemption.

SECTION: 41
HEADING: Elections by taxpayers
1. A taxpayer may make an election only where this Act provides for the election.
2. An election must be made in the manner and by the date required by the applicable provision.
3. An election is binding for the period specified by the provision unless the Commissioner approves a revocation or another provision permits a change.

SECTION: 42
HEADING: Records supporting statutory treatment
1. A person claiming a deduction, credit, exemption, rebate, concession, refund, reduced rate, or other favourable treatment must retain evidence establishing the relevant conditions.
2. Records must be sufficient to permit the Commissioner to verify the amount, period, persons involved, and statutory basis of the treatment.
3. Failure to retain a record does not itself create a tax liability that the Act does not otherwise impose, but may prevent the person from establishing an entitlement where proof is required.

SECTION: 43
HEADING: Changes in circumstances
1. If a fact on which a tax treatment depends changes, the person must make the adjustment required by the applicable provision.
2. A change may include a change in ownership, use, residence, status, classification, consideration, market value, activity, registration, or eligibility.
3. A change occurring after a return is filed may require an amended return or later adjustment if this Act so provides.

SECTION: 44
HEADING: Rates and thresholds
1. A rate or threshold applies from the commencement date specified for it.
2. A rate may be expressed as a percentage, fixed amount, amount per unit, formula, band, or other measure.
3. A threshold may apply to a person, group, transaction, period, amount, volume, value, distance, turnover, or other measure.
4. Unless otherwise provided, a threshold must be tested using the aggregation rules applicable to the relevant regime.

SECTION: 45
HEADING: Regulations and notices
1. Regulations, determinations, notices, and forms made under this Act must be authorised by an express or necessary administrative power.
2. A notice may specify technical requirements for electronic filing, measurement, certification, invoicing, payment, or record keeping.
3. A notice must not alter the substantive liability imposed by this Act.

SECTION: 46
HEADING: Historical application
1. A provision amended, substituted, or repealed after the date on which an amount arose continues to apply where a savings or transitional provision requires it to do so.
2. A reference to a former provision includes the former wording to the extent necessary to determine a liability arising under that provision.
3. The Commissioner may maintain historical records of amendments and their commencement dates.

PARTNUMBER: 4
PARTTITLE: Taxpayer Registration
SECTION: 61
HEADING: Application
1. The Commissioner must administer this provision consistently with the scheme of this Act and having regard to the nature of the income tax to which the provision applies.
2. A person is subject to this provision if the person derives, makes, receives, incurs, holds, uses, transfers, reports, or otherwise deals with an amount, transaction, asset, supply, activity, or circumstance to which the Income Tax rules apply.
3. The relevant amount must be determined after taking into account each adjustment, exemption, credit, deduction, rebate, remission, threshold, or apportionment required by this Act.
   (a) the relevant amount, event, or circumstance must be identified from contemporaneous records;
   (b) each material component of the calculation must be capable of being reconciled to those records;
   (c) any prescribed adjustment must be made before the final amount is reported; and
   (d) the person must retain evidence sufficient to demonstrate why the treatment was adopted.
4. If a matter is partly within the scope of the Income Tax rules and partly within another regime, the amount must be allocated on a reasonable and supportable basis, having regard to the legal form and substance of the transaction.
5. A person relying on an exception or concession must retain records sufficient to establish the facts giving rise to the treatment, including the date, parties, amount, purpose, and supporting calculation.
6. The Commissioner may require further information or make a determination where the information supplied is incomplete, inconsistent with information otherwise available, or insufficient to establish the application of the provision.
   (a) the relevant amount, event, or circumstance must be identified from contemporaneous records;
   (b) each material component of the calculation must be capable of being reconciled to those records;
   (c) any prescribed adjustment must be made before the final amount is reported; and
   (d) the person must retain evidence sufficient to demonstrate why the treatment was adopted.
7. A determination does not prevent a later assessment, reassessment, adjustment, refund, or recovery action where additional facts become available or another provision expressly applies.
SECTION: 62
HEADING: Meaning and scope
1. The Commissioner must administer this provision consistently with the scheme of this Act and having regard to the nature of the goods and services tax to which the provision applies.
2. A person is subject to this provision if the person derives, makes, receives, incurs, holds, uses, transfers, reports, or otherwise deals with an amount, transaction, asset, supply, activity, or circumstance to which the Goods and Services Tax rules apply.
3. The relevant amount must be determined after taking into account each adjustment, exemption, credit, deduction, rebate, remission, threshold, or apportionment required by this Act.
   (a) the relevant amount, event, or circumstance must be identified from contemporaneous records;
   (b) each material component of the calculation must be capable of being reconciled to those records;
   (c) any prescribed adjustment must be made before the final amount is reported; and
   (d) the person must retain evidence sufficient to demonstrate why the treatment was adopted.
4. If a matter is partly within the scope of the Goods and Services Tax rules and partly within another regime, the amount must be allocated on a reasonable and supportable basis, having regard to the legal form and substance of the transaction.
5. A person relying on an exception or concession must retain records sufficient to establish the facts giving rise to the treatment, including the date, parties, amount, purpose, and supporting calculation.
6. The Commissioner may require further information or make a determination where the information supplied is incomplete, inconsistent with information otherwise available, or insufficient to establish the application of the provision.
   (a) the relevant amount, event, or circumstance must be identified from contemporaneous records;
   (b) each material component of the calculation must be capable of being reconciled to those records;
   (c) any prescribed adjustment must be made before the final amount is reported; and
   (d) the person must retain evidence sufficient to demonstrate why the treatment was adopted.
7. A determination does not prevent a later assessment, reassessment, adjustment, refund, or recovery action where additional facts become available or another provision expressly applies.

8. An amount determined under this section is payable, creditable, refundable, or otherwise dealt with at the time specified by this Act, subject to any extension, instalment arrangement, objection, review, or appeal.
9. A provision expressed to apply despite this section prevails to the extent of any inconsistency, but only to the extent necessary to give effect to its stated purpose.
10. The Commissioner must record the basis of a material determination and, where required, give written notice stating the amount, period, reasons, and review rights.
   (a) the relevant amount, event, or circumstance must be identified from contemporaneous records;
   (b) each material component of the calculation must be capable of being reconciled to those records;
   (c) any prescribed adjustment must be made before the final amount is reported; and
   (d) the person must retain evidence sufficient to demonstrate why the treatment was adopted.

5. A person relying on an exception or concession must retain records sufficient to establish the facts giving rise to the treatment, including the date, parties, amount, purpose, and supporting calculation.
6. The Commissioner may require further information or make a determination where the information supplied is incomplete, inconsistent with information otherwise available, or insufficient to establish the application of the provision.
   (a) the relevant circumstance must be established from reliable records;
   (b) the calculation must identify each material component separately; and

4. If a matter is partly within the scope of the Goods and Services Tax rules and partly within another regime, the amount must be allocated on a reasonable and supportable basis, having regard to the legal form and substance of the transaction.
5. A person relying on an exception or concession must retain records sufficient to establish the facts giving rise to the treatment, including the date, parties, amount, purpose, and supporting calculation.
6. The Commissioner may require further information or make a determination where the information supplied is incomplete, inconsistent with information otherwise available, or insufficient to establish the application of the provision.
   (a) the relevant amount, event, or circumstance must be identified from contemporaneous records;
   (b) each material component of the calculation must be capable of being reconciled to those records;
   (c) any prescribed adjustment must be made before the final amount is reported; and
   (d) the person must retain evidence sufficient to demonstrate why the treatment was adopted.
7. A determination does not prevent a later assessment, reassessment, adjustment, refund, or recovery action where additional facts become available or another provision expressly applies.

3. The relevant amount must be determined after taking into account each adjustment, exemption, credit, deduction, rebate, remission, threshold, or apportionment required by this Act.
   (a) the relevant amount, event, or circumstance must be identified from contemporaneous records;
   (b) each material component of the calculation must be capable of being reconciled to those records;
   (c) any prescribed adjustment must be made before the final amount is reported; and
   (d) the person must retain evidence sufficient to demonstrate why the treatment was adopted.
4. If a matter is partly within the scope of the Goods and Services Tax rules and partly within another regime, the amount must be allocated on a reasonable and supportable basis, having regard to the legal form and substance of the transaction.
5. A person relying on an exception or concession must retain records sufficient to establish the facts giving rise to the treatment, including the date, parties, amount, purpose, and supporting calculation.
6. The Commissioner may require further information or make a determination where the information supplied is incomplete, inconsistent with information otherwise available, or insufficient to establish the application of the provision.
   (a) the relevant amount, event, or circumstance must be identified from contemporaneous records;
   (b) each material component of the calculation must be capable of being reconciled to those records;
   (c) any prescribed adjustment must be made before the final amount is reported; and
   (d) the person must retain evidence sufficient to demonstrate why the treatment was adopted.
7. A determination does not prevent a later assessment, reassessment, adjustment, refund, or recovery action where additional facts become available or another provision expressly applies.

2. A person is subject to this provision if the person derives, makes, receives, incurs, holds, uses, transfers, reports, or otherwise deals with an amount, transaction, asset, supply, activity, or circumstance to which the Goods and Services Tax rules apply.
3. The relevant amount must be determined after taking into account each adjustment, exemption, credit, deduction, rebate, remission, threshold, or apportionment required by this Act.
   (a) the relevant amount, event, or circumstance must be identified from contemporaneous records;
   (b) each material component of the calculation must be capable of being reconciled to those records;
   (c) any prescribed adjustment must be made before the final amount is reported; and
   (d) the person must retain evidence sufficient to demonstrate why the treatment was adopted.
4. If a matter is partly within the scope of the Goods and Services Tax rules and partly within another regime, the amount must be allocated on a reasonable and supportable basis, having regard to the legal form and substance of the transaction.
5. A person relying on an exception or concession must retain records sufficient to establish the facts giving rise to the treatment, including the date, parties, amount, purpose, and supporting calculation.
6. The Commissioner may require further information or make a determination where the information supplied is incomplete, inconsistent with information otherwise available, or insufficient to establish the application of the provision.
   (a) the relevant amount, event, or circumstance must be identified from contemporaneous records;
   (b) each material component of the calculation must be capable of being reconciled to those records;
   (c) any prescribed adjustment must be made before the final amount is reported; and
   (d) the person must retain evidence sufficient to demonstrate why the treatment was adopted.
7. A determination does not prevent a later assessment, reassessment, adjustment, refund, or recovery action where additional facts become available or another provision expressly applies.

7. A determination does not prevent a later assessment, reassessment, adjustment, refund, or recovery action where additional facts become available or another provision expressly applies.
8. An amount determined under this section is payable, creditable, refundable, or otherwise dealt with at the time specified by this Act, subject to any extension, instalment arrangement, objection, review, or appeal.
9. A provision expressed to apply despite this section prevails to the extent of any inconsistency, but only to the extent necessary to give effect to its stated purpose.
10. The Commissioner must record the basis of a material determination and, where required, give written notice stating the amount, period, reasons, and review rights.
   (a) the relevant amount, event, or circumstance must be identified from contemporaneous records;
   (b) each material component of the calculation must be capable of being reconciled to those records;
   (c) any prescribed adjustment must be made before the final amount is reported; and
   (d) the person must retain evidence sufficient to demonstrate why the treatment was adopted.
SECTION: 121
HEADING: Interaction with income tax
1. The Commissioner must administer this provision consistently with the scheme of this Act and having regard to the nature of the goods and services tax to which the provision applies.
2. A person is subject to this provision if the person derives, makes, receives, incurs, holds, uses, transfers, reports, or otherwise deals with an amount, transaction, asset, supply, activity, or circumstance to which the Goods and Services Tax rules apply.
3. The relevant amount must be determined after taking into account each adjustment, exemption, credit, deduction, rebate, remission, threshold, or apportionment required by this Act.
   (a) the relevant amount, event, or circumstance must be identified from contemporaneous records;
   (b) each material component of the calculation must be capable of being reconciled to those records;
   (c) any prescribed adjustment must be made before the final amount is reported; and
   (d) the person must retain evidence sufficient to demonstrate why the treatment was adopted.
4. If a matter is partly within the scope of the Goods and Services Tax rules and partly within another regime, the amount must be allocated on a reasonable and supportable basis, having regard to the legal form and substance of the transaction.
5. A person relying on an exception or concession must retain records sufficient to establish the facts giving rise to the treatment, including the date, parties, amount, purpose, and supporting calculation.
6. The Commissioner may require further information or make a determination where the information supplied is incomplete, inconsistent with information otherwise available, or insufficient to establish the application of the provision.
   (a) the relevant amount, event, or circumstance must be identified from contemporaneous records;
   (b) each material component of the calculation must be capable of being reconciled to those records;

9. A provision expressed to apply despite this section prevails to the extent of any inconsistency, but only to the extent necessary to give effect to its stated purpose.
10. The Commissioner must record the basis of a material determination and, where required, give written notice stating the amount, period, reasons, and review rights.
   (a) the relevant amount, event, or circumstance must be identified from contemporaneous records;
   (b) each material component of the calculation must be capable of being reconciled to those records;
   (c) any prescribed adjustment must be made before the final amount is reported; and
   (d) the person must retain evidence sufficient to demonstrate why the treatment was adopted.

HEADING: Failure to comply

   (a) the relevant amount, event, or circumstance must be identified from contemporaneous records;
   (b) each material component of the calculation must be capable of being reconciled to those records;
   (c) any prescribed adjustment must be made before the final amount is reported; and
   (d) the person must retain evidence sufficient to demonstrate why the treatment was adopted.
4. If a matter is partly within the scope of the Income Tax rules and partly within another regime, the amount must be allocated on a reasonable and supportable basis, having regard to the legal form and substance of the transaction.
5. A person relying on an exception or concession must retain records sufficient to establish the facts giving rise to the treatment, including the date, parties, amount, purpose, and supporting calculation.
6. The Commissioner may require further information or make a determination where the information supplied is incomplete, inconsistent with information otherwise available, or insufficient to establish the application of the provision.

5. A person relying on an exception or concession must retain records sufficient to establish the facts giving rise to the treatment, including the date, parties, amount, purpose, and supporting calculation.
6. The Commissioner may require further information or make a determination where the information supplied is incomplete, inconsistent with information otherwise available, or insufficient to establish the application of the provision.
   (a) the relevant circumstance must be established from reliable records;
   (b) the calculation must identify each material component separately; and
   (c) any inconsistency must be corrected or explained in the return or statement.
7. A determination does not prevent a later assessment, reassessment, adjustment, refund, or recovery action where additional facts become available or another provision expressly applies.

5. A person relying on an exception or concession must retain records sufficient to establish the facts giving rise to the treatment, including the date, parties, amount, purpose, and supporting calculation.
6. The Commissioner may require further information or make a determination where the information supplied is incomplete, inconsistent with information otherwise available, or insufficient to establish the application of the provision.
   (a) the relevant amount, event, or circumstance must be identified from contemporaneous records;
   (b) each material component of the calculation must be capable of being reconciled to those records;
   (c) any prescribed adjustment must be made before the final amount is reported; and
   (d) the person must retain evidence sufficient to demonstrate why the treatment was adopted.
7. A determination does not prevent a later assessment, reassessment, adjustment, refund, or recovery action where additional facts become available or another provision expressly applies.

   (c) any prescribed adjustment must be made before the final amount is reported; and
   (d) the person must retain evidence sufficient to demonstrate why the treatment was adopted.
4. If a matter is partly within the scope of the Income Tax rules and partly within another regime, the amount must be allocated on a reasonable and supportable basis, having regard to the legal form and substance of the transaction.
5. A person relying on an exception or concession must retain records sufficient to establish the facts giving rise to the treatment, including the date, parties, amount, purpose, and supporting calculation.
6. The Commissioner may require further information or make a determination where the information supplied is incomplete, inconsistent with information otherwise available, or insufficient to establish the application of the provision.
   (a) the relevant amount, event, or circumstance must be identified from contemporaneous records;
   (b) each material component of the calculation must be capable of being reconciled to those records;
   (c) any prescribed adjustment must be made before the final amount is reported; and
   (d) the person must retain evidence sufficient to demonstrate why the treatment was adopted.
7. A determination does not prevent a later assessment, reassessment, adjustment, refund, or recovery action where additional facts become available or another provision expressly applies.
8. An amount determined under this section is payable, creditable, refundable, or otherwise dealt with at the time specified by this Act, subject to any extension, instalment arrangement, objection, review, or appeal.
9. A provision expressed to apply despite this section prevails to the extent of any inconsistency, but only to the extent necessary to give effect to its stated purpose.

   (a) the relevant circumstance must be established from reliable records;
   (b) the calculation must identify each material component separately; and
   (c) any inconsistency must be corrected or explained in the return or statement.
7. A determination does not prevent a later assessment, reassessment, adjustment, refund, or recovery action where additional facts become available or another provision expressly applies.

   (b) the calculation must identify each material component separately; and
   (c) any inconsistency must be corrected or explained in the return or statement.

SECTION: 224
HEADING: Special rule for agents
1. The Commissioner must administer this provision consistently with the scheme of this Act and having regard to the nature of the income tax to which the provision applies.
2. A person is subject to this provision if the person derives, makes, receives, incurs, holds, uses, transfers, reports, or otherwise deals with an amount, transaction, asset, supply, activity, or circumstance to which the Income Tax rules apply.
3. The relevant amount must be determined after taking into account each adjustment, exemption, credit, deduction, rebate, remission, threshold, or apportionment required by this Act.
   (a) the relevant amount, event, or circumstance must be identified from contemporaneous records;
   (b) each material component of the calculation must be capable of being reconciled to those records;
   (c) any prescribed adjustment must be made before the final amount is reported; and
   (d) the person must retain evidence sufficient to demonstrate why the treatment was adopted.
4. If a matter is partly within the scope of the Income Tax rules and partly within another regime, the amount must be allocated on a reasonable and supportable basis, having regard to the legal form and substance of the transaction.
5. A person relying on an exception or concession must retain records sufficient to establish the facts giving rise to the treatment, including the date, parties, amount, purpose, and supporting calculation.
6. The Commissioner may require further information or make a determination where the information supplied is incomplete, inconsistent with information otherwise available, or insufficient to establish the application of the provision.
   (a) the relevant amount, event, or circumstance must be identified from contemporaneous records;
   (b) each material component of the calculation must be capable of being reconciled to those records;

4. If a matter is partly within the scope of the Company Tax (Large Business) rules and partly within another regime, the amount must be allocated on a reasonable and supportable basis, having regard to the legal form and substance of the transaction.
5. A person relying on an exception or concession must retain records sufficient to establish the facts giving rise to the treatment, including the date, parties, amount, purpose, and supporting calculation.
6. The Commissioner may require further information or make a determination where the information supplied is incomplete, inconsistent with information otherwise available, or insufficient to establish the application of the provision.
   (a) the relevant circumstance must be established from reliable records;
   (b) the calculation must identify each material component separately; and
   (c) any inconsistency must be corrected or explained in the return or statement.
7. A determination does not prevent a later assessment, reassessment, adjustment, refund, or recovery action where additional facts become available or another provision expressly applies.

   (a) the relevant circumstance must be established from reliable records;
   (b) the calculation must identify each material component separately; and
   (c) any inconsistency must be corrected or explained in the return or statement.
4. If a matter is partly within the scope of the Company Tax (Small Business) rules and partly within another regime, the amount must be allocated on a reasonable and supportable basis, having regard to the legal form and substance of the transaction.
5. A person relying on an exception or concession must retain records sufficient to establish the facts giving rise to the treatment, including the date, parties, amount, purpose, and supporting calculation.
6. The Commissioner may require further information or make a determination where the information supplied is incomplete, inconsistent with information otherwise available, or insufficient to establish the application of the provision.
   (a) the relevant circumstance must be established from reliable records;
   (b) the calculation must identify each material component separately; and
   (c) any inconsistency must be corrected or explained in the return or statement.
7. A determination does not prevent a later assessment, reassessment, adjustment, refund, or recovery action where additional facts become available or another provision expressly applies.

SECTION: 257
HEADING: Record of transaction
1. The Commissioner must administer this provision consistently with the scheme of this Act and having regard to the nature of the financial transactions stamp duty (ftsd) to which the provision applies.
2. A person is subject to this provision if the person derives, makes, receives, incurs, holds, uses, transfers, reports, or otherwise deals with an amount, transaction, asset, supply, activity, or circumstance to which the Financial Transactions Stamp Duty (FTSD) rules apply.
3. The relevant amount must be determined after taking into account each adjustment, exemption, credit, deduction, rebate, remission, threshold, or apportionment required by this Act.
   (a) the relevant amount, event, or circumstance must be identified from contemporaneous records;
   (b) each material component of the calculation must be capable of being reconciled to those records;
   (c) any prescribed adjustment must be made before the final amount is reported; and
   (d) the person must retain evidence sufficient to demonstrate why the treatment was adopted.
4. If a matter is partly within the scope of the Financial Transactions Stamp Duty (FTSD) rules and partly within another regime, the amount must be allocated on a reasonable and supportable basis, having regard to the legal form and substance of the transaction.

1. The Commissioner must administer this provision consistently with the scheme of this Act and having regard to the nature of the financial transactions stamp duty (ftsd) to which the provision applies.
2. A person is subject to this provision if the person derives, makes, receives, incurs, holds, uses, transfers, reports, or otherwise deals with an amount, transaction, asset, supply, activity, or circumstance to which the Financial Transactions Stamp Duty (FTSD) rules apply.
3. The relevant amount must be determined after taking into account each adjustment, exemption, credit, deduction, rebate, remission, threshold, or apportionment required by this Act.
   (a) the relevant amount, event, or circumstance must be identified from contemporaneous records;
   (b) each material component of the calculation must be capable of being reconciled to those records;
   (c) any prescribed adjustment must be made before the final amount is reported; and
   (d) the person must retain evidence sufficient to demonstrate why the treatment was adopted.
4. If a matter is partly within the scope of the Financial Transactions Stamp Duty (FTSD) rules and partly within another regime, the amount must be allocated on a reasonable and supportable basis, having regard to the legal form and substance of the transaction.
5. A person relying on an exception or concession must retain records sufficient to establish the facts giving rise to the treatment, including the date, parties, amount, purpose, and supporting calculation.
6. The Commissioner may require further information or make a determination where the information supplied is incomplete, inconsistent with information otherwise available, or insufficient to establish the application of the provision.
   (a) the relevant amount, event, or circumstance must be identified from contemporaneous records;
   (b) each material component of the calculation must be capable of being reconciled to those records;
   (c) any prescribed adjustment must be made before the final amount is reported; and
   (d) the person must retain evidence sufficient to demonstrate why the treatment was adopted.
7. A determination does not prevent a later assessment, reassessment, adjustment, refund, or recovery action where additional facts become available or another provision expressly applies.

6. The Commissioner may require further information or make a determination where the information supplied is incomplete, inconsistent with information otherwise available, or insufficient to establish the application of the provision.
   (a) the relevant amount, event, or circumstance must be identified from contemporaneous records;
   (b) each material component of the calculation must be capable of being reconciled to those records;
   (c) any prescribed adjustment must be made before the final amount is reported; and
   (d) the person must retain evidence sufficient to demonstrate why the treatment was adopted.
7. A determination does not prevent a later assessment, reassessment, adjustment, refund, or recovery action where additional facts become available or another provision expressly applies.
8. An amount determined under this section is payable, creditable, refundable, or otherwise dealt with at the time specified by this Act, subject to any extension, instalment arrangement, objection, review, or appeal.
9. A provision expressed to apply despite this section prevails to the extent of any inconsistency, but only to the extent necessary to give effect to its stated purpose.
10. The Commissioner must record the basis of a material determination and, where required, give written notice stating the amount, period, reasons, and review rights.
   (a) the relevant amount, event, or circumstance must be identified from contemporaneous records;
   (b) each material component of the calculation must be capable of being reconciled to those records;
   (c) any prescribed adjustment must be made before the final amount is reported; and
   (d) the person must retain evidence sufficient to demonstrate why the treatment was adopted.

6. The Commissioner may require further information or make a determination where the information supplied is incomplete, inconsistent with information otherwise available, or insufficient to establish the application of the provision.
   (a) the relevant amount, event, or circumstance must be identified from contemporaneous records;
   (b) each material component of the calculation must be capable of being reconciled to those records;
   (c) any prescribed adjustment must be made before the final amount is reported; and
   (d) the person must retain evidence sufficient to demonstrate why the treatment was adopted.
7. A determination does not prevent a later assessment, reassessment, adjustment, refund, or recovery action where additional facts become available or another provision expressly applies.
8. An amount determined under this section is payable, creditable, refundable, or otherwise dealt with at the time specified by this Act, subject to any extension, instalment arrangement, objection, review, or appeal.
9. A provision expressed to apply despite this section prevails to the extent of any inconsistency, but only to the extent necessary to give effect to its stated purpose.
10. The Commissioner must record the basis of a material determination and, where required, give written notice stating the amount, period, reasons, and review rights.
   (a) the relevant amount, event, or circumstance must be identified from contemporaneous records;
   (b) each material component of the calculation must be capable of being reconciled to those records;
   (c) any prescribed adjustment must be made before the final amount is reported; and
   (d) the person must retain evidence sufficient to demonstrate why the treatment was adopted.

5. A person relying on an exception or concession must retain records sufficient to establish the facts giving rise to the treatment, including the date, parties, amount, purpose, and supporting calculation.
6. The Commissioner may require further information or make a determination where the information supplied is incomplete, inconsistent with information otherwise available, or insufficient to establish the application of the provision.
   (a) the relevant circumstance must be established from reliable records;
   (b) the calculation must identify each material component separately; and
   (c) any inconsistency must be corrected or explained in the return or statement.
7. A determination does not prevent a later assessment, reassessment, adjustment, refund, or recovery action where additional facts become available or another provision expressly applies.

4. If a matter is partly within the scope of the Digital Platform Services Tax (DPST) rules and partly within another regime, the amount must be allocated on a reasonable and supportable basis, having regard to the legal form and substance of the transaction.
5. A person relying on an exception or concession must retain records sufficient to establish the facts giving rise to the treatment, including the date, parties, amount, purpose, and supporting calculation.
6. The Commissioner may require further information or make a determination where the information supplied is incomplete, inconsistent with information otherwise available, or insufficient to establish the application of the provision.
   (a) the relevant amount, event, or circumstance must be identified from contemporaneous records;
   (b) each material component of the calculation must be capable of being reconciled to those records;
   (c) any prescribed adjustment must be made before the final amount is reported; and
   (d) the person must retain evidence sufficient to demonstrate why the treatment was adopted.
7. A determination does not prevent a later assessment, reassessment, adjustment, refund, or recovery action where additional facts become available or another provision expressly applies.
8. An amount determined under this section is payable, creditable, refundable, or otherwise dealt with at the time specified by this Act, subject to any extension, instalment arrangement, objection, review, or appeal.
9. A provision expressed to apply despite this section prevails to the extent of any inconsistency, but only to the extent necessary to give effect to its stated purpose.
10. The Commissioner must record the basis of a material determination and, where required, give written notice stating the amount, period, reasons, and review rights.
   (a) the relevant amount, event, or circumstance must be identified from contemporaneous records;
   (b) each material component of the calculation must be capable of being reconciled to those records;
   (c) any prescribed adjustment must be made before the final amount is reported; and
   (d) the person must retain evidence sufficient to demonstrate why the treatment was adopted.

4. If a matter is partly within the scope of the Private Natural Resource Extraction Levy (FWEL) rules and partly within another regime, the amount must be allocated on a reasonable and supportable basis, having regard to the legal form and substance of the transaction.
5. A person relying on an exception or concession must retain records sufficient to establish the facts giving rise to the treatment, including the date, parties, amount, purpose, and supporting calculation.
6. The Commissioner may require further information or make a determination where the information supplied is incomplete, inconsistent with information otherwise available, or insufficient to establish the application of the provision.
   (a) the relevant amount, event, or circumstance must be identified from contemporaneous records;
   (b) each material component of the calculation must be capable of being reconciled to those records;
   (c) any prescribed adjustment must be made before the final amount is reported; and
   (d) the person must retain evidence sufficient to demonstrate why the treatment was adopted.
7. A determination does not prevent a later assessment, reassessment, adjustment, refund, or recovery action where additional facts become available or another provision expressly applies.

   (d) the person must retain evidence sufficient to demonstrate why the treatment was adopted.

8. An amount determined under this section is payable, creditable, refundable, or otherwise dealt with at the time specified by this Act, subject to any extension, instalment arrangement, objection, review, or appeal.
9. A provision expressed to apply despite this section prevails to the extent of any inconsistency, but only to the extent necessary to give effect to its stated purpose.
10. The Commissioner must record the basis of a material determination and, where required, give written notice stating the amount, period, reasons, and review rights.
   (a) the relevant amount, event, or circumstance must be identified from contemporaneous records;
   (b) each material component of the calculation must be capable of being reconciled to those records;
   (c) any prescribed adjustment must be made before the final amount is reported; and
   (d) the person must retain evidence sufficient to demonstrate why the treatment was adopted.
SECTION: 355B
HEADING: Commissioner’s discretion
1. The Commissioner must administer this provision consistently with the scheme of this Act and having regard to the nature of the fuel excise duty (fed) to which the provision applies.
2. A person is subject to this provision if the person derives, makes, receives, incurs, holds, uses, transfers, reports, or otherwise deals with an amount, transaction, asset, supply, activity, or circumstance to which the Fuel Excise Duty (FED) rules apply.
3. The relevant amount must be determined after taking into account each adjustment, exemption, credit, deduction, rebate, remission, threshold, or apportionment required by this Act.
   (a) the relevant circumstance must be established from reliable records;
   (b) the calculation must identify each material component separately; and
   (c) any inconsistency must be corrected or explained in the return or statement.
4. If a matter is partly within the scope of the Fuel Excise Duty (FED) rules and partly within another regime, the amount must be allocated on a reasonable and supportable basis, having regard to the legal form and substance of the transaction.
5. A person relying on an exception or concession must retain records sufficient to establish the facts giving rise to the treatment, including the date, parties, amount, purpose, and supporting calculation.
6. The Commissioner may require further information or make a determination where the information supplied is incomplete, inconsistent with information otherwise available, or insufficient to establish the application of the provision.
   (a) the relevant circumstance must be established from reliable records;
   (b) the calculation must identify each material component separately; and
   (c) any inconsistency must be corrected or explained in the return or statement.
7. A determination does not prevent a later assessment, reassessment, adjustment, refund, or recovery action where additional facts become available or another provision expressly applies.

4. If a matter is partly within the scope of the Road User Charges (RUC) rules and partly within another regime, the amount must be allocated on a reasonable and supportable basis, having regard to the legal form and substance of the transaction.
5. A person relying on an exception or concession must retain records sufficient to establish the facts giving rise to the treatment, including the date, parties, amount, purpose, and supporting calculation.
6. The Commissioner may require further information or make a determination where the information supplied is incomplete, inconsistent with information otherwise available, or insufficient to establish the application of the provision.
   (a) the relevant circumstance must be established from reliable records;
   (b) the calculation must identify each material component separately; and
   (c) any inconsistency must be corrected or explained in the return or statement.
7. A determination does not prevent a later assessment, reassessment, adjustment, refund, or recovery action where additional facts become available or another provision expressly applies.

2. A person is subject to this provision if the person derives, makes, receives, incurs, holds, uses, transfers, reports, or otherwise deals with an amount, transaction, asset, supply, activity, or circumstance to which the Fuel Excise Duty (FED) rules apply.
3. The relevant amount must be determined after taking into account each adjustment, exemption, credit, deduction, rebate, remission, threshold, or apportionment required by this Act.
   (a) the relevant circumstance must be established from reliable records;
   (b) the calculation must identify each material component separately; and
   (c) any inconsistency must be corrected or explained in the return or statement.
4. If a matter is partly within the scope of the Fuel Excise Duty (FED) rules and partly within another regime, the amount must be allocated on a reasonable and supportable basis, having regard to the legal form and substance of the transaction.
5. A person relying on an exception or concession must retain records sufficient to establish the facts giving rise to the treatment, including the date, parties, amount, purpose, and supporting calculation.
6. The Commissioner may require further information or make a determination where the information supplied is incomplete, inconsistent with information otherwise available, or insufficient to establish the application of the provision.
   (a) the relevant circumstance must be established from reliable records;
   (b) the calculation must identify each material component separately; and
   (c) any inconsistency must be corrected or explained in the return or statement.
7. A determination does not prevent a later assessment, reassessment, adjustment, refund, or recovery action where additional facts become available or another provision expressly applies.

4. If a matter is partly within the scope of the Alcohol Excise rules and partly within another regime, the amount must be allocated on a reasonable and supportable basis, having regard to the legal form and substance of the transaction.
5. A person relying on an exception or concession must retain records sufficient to establish the facts giving rise to the treatment, including the date, parties, amount, purpose, and supporting calculation.
6. The Commissioner may require further information or make a determination where the information supplied is incomplete, inconsistent with information otherwise available, or insufficient to establish the application of the provision.
   (a) the relevant amount, event, or circumstance must be identified from contemporaneous records;
   (b) each material component of the calculation must be capable of being reconciled to those records;
   (c) any prescribed adjustment must be made before the final amount is reported; and
   (d) the person must retain evidence sufficient to demonstrate why the treatment was adopted.
7. A determination does not prevent a later assessment, reassessment, adjustment, refund, or recovery action where additional facts become available or another provision expressly applies.
8. An amount determined under this section is payable, creditable, refundable, or otherwise dealt with at the time specified by this Act, subject to any extension, instalment arrangement, objection, review, or appeal.
9. A provision expressed to apply despite this section prevails to the extent of any inconsistency, but only to the extent necessary to give effect to its stated purpose.
10. The Commissioner must record the basis of a material determination and, where required, give written notice stating the amount, period, reasons, and review rights.
   (a) the relevant amount, event, or circumstance must be identified from contemporaneous records;
   (b) each material component of the calculation must be capable of being reconciled to those records;
   (c) any prescribed adjustment must be made before the final amount is reported; and
   (d) the person must retain evidence sufficient to demonstrate why the treatment was adopted.

SECTION: 407
HEADING: Electronic payment
1. The Commissioner must administer this provision consistently with the scheme of this Act and having regard to the nature of the customs & duty to which the provision applies.
2. A person is subject to this provision if the person derives, makes, receives, incurs, holds, uses, transfers, reports, or otherwise deals with an amount, transaction, asset, supply, activity, or circumstance to which the Customs & Duty rules apply.
3. The relevant amount must be determined after taking into account each adjustment, exemption, credit, deduction, rebate, remission, threshold, or apportionment required by this Act.
   (a) the relevant amount, event, or circumstance must be identified from contemporaneous records;
   (b) each material component of the calculation must be capable of being reconciled to those records;
   (c) any prescribed adjustment must be made before the final amount is reported; and
   (d) the person must retain evidence sufficient to demonstrate why the treatment was adopted.
4. If a matter is partly within the scope of the Customs & Duty rules and partly within another regime, the amount must be allocated on a reasonable and supportable basis, having regard to the legal form and substance of the transaction.
5. A person relying on an exception or concession must retain records sufficient to establish the facts giving rise to the treatment, including the date, parties, amount, purpose, and supporting calculation.
6. The Commissioner may require further information or make a determination where the information supplied is incomplete, inconsistent with information otherwise available, or insufficient to establish the application of the provision.
   (a) the relevant amount, event, or circumstance must be identified from contemporaneous records;

   (d) the person must retain evidence sufficient to demonstrate why the treatment was adopted.
7. A determination does not prevent a later assessment, reassessment, adjustment, refund, or recovery action where additional facts become available or another provision expressly applies.
SECTION: 418B
HEADING: Offence
1. The Commissioner must administer this provision consistently with the scheme of this Act and having regard to the nature of the customs & duty to which the provision applies.
2. A person is subject to this provision if the person derives, makes, receives, incurs, holds, uses, transfers, reports, or otherwise deals with an amount, transaction, asset, supply, activity, or circumstance to which the Customs & Duty rules apply.
3. The relevant amount must be determined after taking into account each adjustment, exemption, credit, deduction, rebate, remission, threshold, or apportionment required by this Act.
   (a) the relevant circumstance must be established from reliable records;
   (b) the calculation must identify each material component separately; and
   (c) any inconsistency must be corrected or explained in the return or statement.
4. If a matter is partly within the scope of the Customs & Duty rules and partly within another regime, the amount must be allocated on a reasonable and supportable basis, having regard to the legal form and substance of the transaction.
5. A person relying on an exception or concession must retain records sufficient to establish the facts giving rise to the treatment, including the date, parties, amount, purpose, and supporting calculation.
6. The Commissioner may require further information or make a determination where the information supplied is incomplete, inconsistent with information otherwise available, or insufficient to establish the application of the provision.
   (a) the relevant circumstance must be established from reliable records;
   (b) the calculation must identify each material component separately; and
   (c) any inconsistency must be corrected or explained in the return or statement.
7. A determination does not prevent a later assessment, reassessment, adjustment, refund, or recovery action where additional facts become available or another provision expressly applies.

SECTION: 427DA
HEADING: Time of liability
1. The Commissioner must administer this provision consistently with the scheme of this Act and having regard to the nature of the revenue from state assets to which the provision applies.
2. A person is subject to this provision if the person derives, makes, receives, incurs, holds, uses, transfers, reports, or otherwise deals with an amount, transaction, asset, supply, activity, or circumstance to which the Revenue from State Assets rules apply.
3. The relevant amount must be determined after taking into account each adjustment, exemption, credit, deduction, rebate, remission, threshold, or apportionment required by this Act.
   (a) the relevant circumstance must be established from reliable records;
   (b) the calculation must identify each material component separately; and
   (c) any inconsistency must be corrected or explained in the return or statement.
4. If a matter is partly within the scope of the Revenue from State Assets rules and partly within another regime, the amount must be allocated on a reasonable and supportable basis, having regard to the legal form and substance of the transaction.

SECTION: 438
HEADING: Correction of assessment
1. The Commissioner must administer this provision consistently with the scheme of this Act and having regard to the nature of the revenue from state assets to which the provision applies.

   (a) the relevant amount, event, or circumstance must be identified from contemporaneous records;
   (b) each material component of the calculation must be capable of being reconciled to those records;
   (c) any prescribed adjustment must be made before the final amount is reported; and
   (d) the person must retain evidence sufficient to demonstrate why the treatment was adopted.

6. The Commissioner may require further information or make a determination where the information supplied is incomplete, inconsistent with information otherwise available, or insufficient to establish the application of the provision.
   (a) the relevant amount, event, or circumstance must be identified from contemporaneous records;
