1. The Commissioner must administer this provision consistently with the scheme of this Act and having regard to the nature of the financial transactions stamp duty (ftsd) to which the provision applies.
2. A person is subject to this provision if the person derives, makes, receives, incurs, holds, uses, transfers, reports, or otherwise deals with an amount, transaction, asset, supply, activity, or circumstance to which the Financial Transactions Stamp Duty (FTSD) rules apply.
3. The relevant amount must be determined after taking into account each adjustment, exemption, credit, deduction, rebate, remission, threshold, or apportionment required by this Act.
   (a) the relevant amount, event, or circumstance must be identified from contemporaneous records;
   (b) each material component of the calculation must be capable of being reconciled to those records;
   (c) any prescribed adjustment must be made before the final amount is reported; and
   (d) the person must retain evidence sufficient to demonstrate why the treatment was adopted.
4. If a matter is partly within the scope of the Financial Transactions Stamp Duty (FTSD) rules and partly within another regime, the amount must be allocated on a reasonable and supportable basis, having regard to the legal form and substance of the transaction.
5. A person relying on an exception or concession must retain records sufficient to establish the facts giving rise to the treatment, including the date, parties, amount, purpose, and supporting calculation.
6. The Commissioner may require further information or make a determination where the information supplied is incomplete, inconsistent with information otherwise available, or insufficient to establish the application of the provision.
   (a) the relevant amount, event, or circumstance must be identified from contemporaneous records;
   (b) each material component of the calculation must be capable of being reconciled to those records;
   (c) any prescribed adjustment must be made before the final amount is reported; and
   (d) the person must retain evidence sufficient to demonstrate why the treatment was adopted.
7. A determination does not prevent a later assessment, reassessment, adjustment, refund, or recovery action where additional facts become available or another provision expressly applies.

5. A person relying on an exception or concession must retain records sufficient to establish the facts giving rise to the treatment, including the date, parties, amount, purpose, and supporting calculation.
6. The Commissioner may require further information or make a determination where the information supplied is incomplete, inconsistent with information otherwise available, or insufficient to establish the application of the provision.
   (a) the relevant amount, event, or circumstance must be identified from contemporaneous records;
   (b) each material component of the calculation must be capable of being reconciled to those records;
   (c) any prescribed adjustment must be made before the final amount is reported; and
   (d) the person must retain evidence sufficient to demonstrate why the treatment was adopted.
7. A determination does not prevent a later assessment, reassessment, adjustment, refund, or recovery action where additional facts become available or another provision expressly applies.

   (c) any inconsistency must be corrected or explained in the return or statement.

3. The relevant amount must be determined after taking into account each adjustment, exemption, credit, deduction, rebate, remission, threshold, or apportionment required by this Act.
   (a) the relevant amount, event, or circumstance must be identified from contemporaneous records;
   (b) each material component of the calculation must be capable of being reconciled to those records;
   (c) any prescribed adjustment must be made before the final amount is reported; and
   (d) the person must retain evidence sufficient to demonstrate why the treatment was adopted.
4. If a matter is partly within the scope of the Income Tax rules and partly within another regime, the amount must be allocated on a reasonable and supportable basis, having regard to the legal form and substance of the transaction.
5. A person relying on an exception or concession must retain records sufficient to establish the facts giving rise to the treatment, including the date, parties, amount, purpose, and supporting calculation.
6. The Commissioner may require further information or make a determination where the information supplied is incomplete, inconsistent with information otherwise available, or insufficient to establish the application of the provision.
   (a) the relevant amount, event, or circumstance must be identified from contemporaneous records;
   (b) each material component of the calculation must be capable of being reconciled to those records;
   (c) any prescribed adjustment must be made before the final amount is reported; and
   (d) the person must retain evidence sufficient to demonstrate why the treatment was adopted.
7. A determination does not prevent a later assessment, reassessment, adjustment, refund, or recovery action where additional facts become available or another provision expressly applies.
8. An amount determined under this section is payable, creditable, refundable, or otherwise dealt with at the time specified by this Act, subject to any extension, instalment arrangement, objection, review, or appeal.
9. A provision expressed to apply despite this section prevails to the extent of any inconsistency, but only to the extent necessary to give effect to its stated purpose.
10. The Commissioner must record the basis of a material determination and, where required, give written notice stating the amount, period, reasons, and review rights.
   (a) the relevant amount, event, or circumstance must be identified from contemporaneous records;
   (b) each material component of the calculation must be capable of being reconciled to those records;
   (c) any prescribed adjustment must be made before the final amount is reported; and
   (d) the person must retain evidence sufficient to demonstrate why the treatment was adopted.

2. A person is subject to this provision if the person derives, makes, receives, incurs, holds, uses, transfers, reports, or otherwise deals with an amount, transaction, asset, supply, activity, or circumstance to which the Revenue from State Assets rules apply.
3. The relevant amount must be determined after taking into account each adjustment, exemption, credit, deduction, rebate, remission, threshold, or apportionment required by this Act.
   (a) the relevant amount, event, or circumstance must be identified from contemporaneous records;
   (b) each material component of the calculation must be capable of being reconciled to those records;
   (c) any prescribed adjustment must be made before the final amount is reported; and
   (d) the person must retain evidence sufficient to demonstrate why the treatment was adopted.
4. If a matter is partly within the scope of the Revenue from State Assets rules and partly within another regime, the amount must be allocated on a reasonable and supportable basis, having regard to the legal form and substance of the transaction.
5. A person relying on an exception or concession must retain records sufficient to establish the facts giving rise to the treatment, including the date, parties, amount, purpose, and supporting calculation.
6. The Commissioner may require further information or make a determination where the information supplied is incomplete, inconsistent with information otherwise available, or insufficient to establish the application of the provision.
   (a) the relevant amount, event, or circumstance must be identified from contemporaneous records;
   (b) each material component of the calculation must be capable of being reconciled to those records;
   (c) any prescribed adjustment must be made before the final amount is reported; and
   (d) the person must retain evidence sufficient to demonstrate why the treatment was adopted.
7. A determination does not prevent a later assessment, reassessment, adjustment, refund, or recovery action where additional facts become available or another provision expressly applies.

2. A person is subject to this provision if the person derives, makes, receives, incurs, holds, uses, transfers, reports, or otherwise deals with an amount, transaction, asset, supply, activity, or circumstance to which the Revenue from State Assets rules apply.
3. The relevant amount must be determined after taking into account each adjustment, exemption, credit, deduction, rebate, remission, threshold, or apportionment required by this Act.
   (a) the relevant circumstance must be established from reliable records;
   (b) the calculation must identify each material component separately; and
   (c) any inconsistency must be corrected or explained in the return or statement.
4. If a matter is partly within the scope of the Revenue from State Assets rules and partly within another regime, the amount must be allocated on a reasonable and supportable basis, having regard to the legal form and substance of the transaction.
5. A person relying on an exception or concession must retain records sufficient to establish the facts giving rise to the treatment, including the date, parties, amount, purpose, and supporting calculation.
6. The Commissioner may require further information or make a determination where the information supplied is incomplete, inconsistent with information otherwise available, or insufficient to establish the application of the provision.
   (a) the relevant circumstance must be established from reliable records;
   (b) the calculation must identify each material component separately; and
   (c) any inconsistency must be corrected or explained in the return or statement.
7. A determination does not prevent a later assessment, reassessment, adjustment, refund, or recovery action where additional facts become available or another provision expressly applies.

SECTION: 1004
HEADING: Alternative method
1. The Commissioner must administer this provision consistently with the scheme of this Act and having regard to the nature of the income tax to which the provision applies.
2. A person is subject to this provision if the person derives, makes, receives, incurs, holds, uses, transfers, reports, or otherwise deals with an amount, transaction, asset, supply, activity, or circumstance to which the Income Tax rules apply.

   (a) the relevant amount, event, or circumstance must be identified from contemporaneous records;
   (b) each material component of the calculation must be capable of being reconciled to those records;
   (c) any prescribed adjustment must be made before the final amount is reported; and
   (d) the person must retain evidence sufficient to demonstrate why the treatment was adopted.

6. The Commissioner may require further information or make a determination where the information supplied is incomplete, inconsistent with information otherwise available, or insufficient to establish the application of the provision.
   (a) the relevant amount, event, or circumstance must be identified from contemporaneous records;
   (b) each material component of the calculation must be capable of being reconciled to those records;
   (c) any prescribed adjustment must be made before the final amount is reported; and

SECTION: 1014
HEADING: Instalment arrangement
1. The Commissioner must administer this provision consistently with the scheme of this Act and having regard to the nature of the income tax to which the provision applies.
2. A person is subject to this provision if the person derives, makes, receives, incurs, holds, uses, transfers, reports, or otherwise deals with an amount, transaction, asset, supply, activity, or circumstance to which the Income Tax rules apply.
3. The relevant amount must be determined after taking into account each adjustment, exemption, credit, deduction, rebate, remission, threshold, or apportionment required by this Act.
   (a) the relevant amount, event, or circumstance must be identified from contemporaneous records;
   (b) each material component of the calculation must be capable of being reconciled to those records;
   (c) any prescribed adjustment must be made before the final amount is reported; and
   (d) the person must retain evidence sufficient to demonstrate why the treatment was adopted.
4. If a matter is partly within the scope of the Income Tax rules and partly within another regime, the amount must be allocated on a reasonable and supportable basis, having regard to the legal form and substance of the transaction.
5. A person relying on an exception or concession must retain records sufficient to establish the facts giving rise to the treatment, including the date, parties, amount, purpose, and supporting calculation.
6. The Commissioner may require further information or make a determination where the information supplied is incomplete, inconsistent with information otherwise available, or insufficient to establish the application of the provision.
   (a) the relevant amount, event, or circumstance must be identified from contemporaneous records;
   (b) each material component of the calculation must be capable of being reconciled to those records;
   (c) any prescribed adjustment must be made before the final amount is reported; and
   (d) the person must retain evidence sufficient to demonstrate why the treatment was adopted.
7. A determination does not prevent a later assessment, reassessment, adjustment, refund, or recovery action where additional facts become available or another provision expressly applies.

3. The relevant amount must be determined after taking into account each adjustment, exemption, credit, deduction, rebate, remission, threshold, or apportionment required by this Act.
   (a) the relevant amount, event, or circumstance must be identified from contemporaneous records;
   (b) each material component of the calculation must be capable of being reconciled to those records;
   (c) any prescribed adjustment must be made before the final amount is reported; and
   (d) the person must retain evidence sufficient to demonstrate why the treatment was adopted.
4. If a matter is partly within the scope of the Income Tax rules and partly within another regime, the amount must be allocated on a reasonable and supportable basis, having regard to the legal form and substance of the transaction.
5. A person relying on an exception or concession must retain records sufficient to establish the facts giving rise to the treatment, including the date, parties, amount, purpose, and supporting calculation.
6. The Commissioner may require further information or make a determination where the information supplied is incomplete, inconsistent with information otherwise available, or insufficient to establish the application of the provision.
   (a) the relevant amount, event, or circumstance must be identified from contemporaneous records;
   (b) each material component of the calculation must be capable of being reconciled to those records;
   (c) any prescribed adjustment must be made before the final amount is reported; and
   (d) the person must retain evidence sufficient to demonstrate why the treatment was adopted.
7. A determination does not prevent a later assessment, reassessment, adjustment, refund, or recovery action where additional facts become available or another provision expressly applies.

   (a) the relevant amount, event, or circumstance must be identified from contemporaneous records;
   (b) each material component of the calculation must be capable of being reconciled to those records;
   (c) any prescribed adjustment must be made before the final amount is reported; and
   (d) the person must retain evidence sufficient to demonstrate why the treatment was adopted.
4. If a matter is partly within the scope of the Income Tax rules and partly within another regime, the amount must be allocated on a reasonable and supportable basis, having regard to the legal form and substance of the transaction.
5. A person relying on an exception or concession must retain records sufficient to establish the facts giving rise to the treatment, including the date, parties, amount, purpose, and supporting calculation.
6. The Commissioner may require further information or make a determination where the information supplied is incomplete, inconsistent with information otherwise available, or insufficient to establish the application of the provision.
   (a) the relevant amount, event, or circumstance must be identified from contemporaneous records;
   (b) each material component of the calculation must be capable of being reconciled to those records;
   (c) any prescribed adjustment must be made before the final amount is reported; and
   (d) the person must retain evidence sufficient to demonstrate why the treatment was adopted.
7. A determination does not prevent a later assessment, reassessment, adjustment, refund, or recovery action where additional facts become available or another provision expressly applies.

10. The Commissioner must record the basis of a material determination and, where required, give written notice stating the amount, period, reasons, and review rights.
   (a) the relevant amount, event, or circumstance must be identified from contemporaneous records;
   (b) each material component of the calculation must be capable of being reconciled to those records;
   (c) any prescribed adjustment must be made before the final amount is reported; and
   (d) the person must retain evidence sufficient to demonstrate why the treatment was adopted.

5. A person relying on an exception or concession must retain records sufficient to establish the facts giving rise to the treatment, including the date, parties, amount, purpose, and supporting calculation.
6. The Commissioner may require further information or make a determination where the information supplied is incomplete, inconsistent with information otherwise available, or insufficient to establish the application of the provision.
   (a) the relevant amount, event, or circumstance must be identified from contemporaneous records;
   (b) each material component of the calculation must be capable of being reconciled to those records;
   (c) any prescribed adjustment must be made before the final amount is reported; and
   (d) the person must retain evidence sufficient to demonstrate why the treatment was adopted.
7. A determination does not prevent a later assessment, reassessment, adjustment, refund, or recovery action where additional facts become available or another provision expressly applies.

SECTION: 1239
HEADING: Transitional application
1. The principal revenue sources administered under this Act are—
   (a) Income Tax;
   (b) Goods and Services Tax;
   (c) Digital Platform Services Tax (DPST);
   (d) Financial Transactions Stamp Duty (FTSD);
   (e) Private Natural Resource Extraction Levy (FWEL);
   (f) Natural Water Resource Use Levy;
   (g) ETS Revenue;
   (h) Universal Financial Services Excise;
   (i) Company Tax (Large Business);
   (j) Company Tax (Small Business);
   (k) Infrastructure Contribution Levy (ICL);
   (l) Fuel Excise Duty (FED);
   (m) Road User Charges (RUC);
   (n) Tobacco Excise;
   (o) Alcohol Excise;
   (p) IRCC Levies;
   (q) Collecting Tax Evasion;
   (r) Customs & Duty;
   (s) Waste Disposal Levy; and
   (t) Revenue from State Assets.
2. Nothing in this section by itself imposes a tax, duty, levy, excise, or charge; liability arises under the operative provision establishing that liability.
3. A reference to a revenue source includes its associated assessment, collection, credit, refund, rebate, interest, penalty, reporting, and recovery provisions unless the context requires otherwise.
